title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Statistical Systems Out of Equilibrium
authors: Weam Abou Hamdan, Martí Berenguer Mimó, Rafael Carrasco Carmona, Silvia Pla, Omkar Shetye, Tarek Anous, Paolo Benincasa, Guilherme Leite Pimentel
abstract: These lecture notes provide an introduction to quantum spin glasses, with a particular emphasis on their application to open problems in cosmology and holography. Focusing on the spherical $p$-spin model, we develop a complete and self-contained analysis of its thermodynamic and dynamical properties. We introduce the replica method, discuss both replica-symmetric and one-step replica symmetry-broken solutions, and characterise the resulting glassy phase. The framework is then extended to the quantum model, where we study the emergence of slow dynamics and the role of quantum correlations through Euclidean and real-time correlation functions. Finally, we explore how concepts such as replica symmetry breaking and disorder naturally arise in cosmological and holographic systems related to black hole fragmentation, highlighting spin glass models as useful theoretical laboratories for these phenomena. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School: The Disordered Universe 2025 from 21 July to 1 August 2025.
summary: This work provides a comprehensive theoretical analysis of quantum spin glasses using the spherical p-spin model. It develops techniques like the replica method and RSB to characterize the glassy phase transition. The findings are crucial as they establish spin glass models as powerful theoretical laboratories for understanding disorder in complex physical regimes, including cosmology and holography.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical characterization of the glass transition in disordered systems, extending concepts from spin glasses to cosmology and holography.
main_result: It derives the thermodynamic and dynamic properties of the spherical p-spin model, showing a clear transition from a high-temperature paramagnetic phase to a low-temperature glassy phase characterized by spontaneous magnetization.
method: The analysis heavily relies on the replica method and replica symmetry breaking (RSB) techniques, combined with mean-field approximations and saddle-point evaluations in the large-N limit.
model_or_system: The primary model is the spherical p-spin glass, which captures frustration and quenched disorder. The framework is then applied conceptually to cosmological and holographic systems related to black hole fragmentation.
key_observables: Free energy per site, magnetization ($\langle m angle$), susceptibility ($\chi$), and real-time correlation functions.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), coupling constant ($J$), and the dimensionality parameter $p$ of the spin interaction.
main_assumptions: The calculations are performed in the mean-field approximation and rely on the large-N limit and saddle-point approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the free energy landscape changing from a single minimum to two symmetric minima upon cooling, and show the divergence of susceptibility at the critical temperature.
paper_structure: The structure moves from classical spin glass analysis (mean-field, replica method) to the quantum extension, detailing the calculation of thermodynamic quantities and finally connecting the mathematical formalism to physical concepts in cosmology and holography.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical tools developed for spin glasses (RSB, free energy landscapes) provide powerful, transferable frameworks for understanding complex, out-of-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
